text:
maya: heads-up — customer on private (VPC) deployment reporting traffic for their us-east-1 tenant is hitting our eu proxy and failing auth. they pin region in app config. logs show X-Forwarded-For preserved and x-redwood-region: us-east-1 but requests land in eu-lb and get 401. anyone seen this pattern?
raj: can you paste the original HTTP headers + a short traceroute from the customer's bastion? also which NAT/peering topology are they using?
maya: pasted headers below and traceroute. small snippets:

----- HEADERS -----
host: api.redwood.example
x-redwood-region: us-east-1
x-customer-id: cust-42
x-forwarded-for: 10.0.12.5
authorization: Bearer <token>
-------------------

traceroute to api.redwood.example (35.180.12.9), 30 hops max:
 1  10.0.0.1  0.6 ms
 2  192.168.254.1  1.2 ms
 3  100.64.0.5  12.3 ms  (peering-hub-us-east)
 4  52.18.100.2  20.4 ms  (edge-us-east)
 5  34.242.80.200  85.7 ms  (edge-eu)

maya: note hop 5 jumps to eu. customer topology: on-prem -> managed-VPN -> hub-peering -> regional egress. they use NAT on hub.
eli: my suspicion: SNAT/NAT hairpin at the peering hub is rewriting source or forcing return path to EU NAT due to asymmetric route selection (BGP + MED/LOCAL_PREF). when NAT session gets established via hub that prefers eu path, subsequent packets go out eu LB. check conntrack/NAT table timeouts and SNAT IP allocation per region.
netops: looking at peering tables now — i see the hub has dynamic NAT pools with no region affinity. some flows are SNATted to a floating public IP that announces from our eu cluster because of a BGP path preference leak after a recent failover.
raj: can you run on the customer's bastion:

```
# check route to our public IP
ip route get 35.180.12.9
# do a curl forcing our IP to resolve to us-east edge
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example:443:35.180.12.9 https://api.redwood.example/health
# tcp traceroute
tcptraceroute 35.180.12.9 443
```

maya: they ran those. ip route get shows next-hop via peering-hub-us-east, but tcptraceroute shows an AS hop into eu-edge. curl gets TCP established then HTTP 401 from eu-edge with header x-region-served: eu-central-1.
support-bot: filing internal incident INC-4052 and tagging #netops #infra. template: escalated private egress -> wrong-region; customer impact: auth failures + increased latency.
eli: short-term mitigation: add a proxy rewrite rule to prefer region from x-redwood-region header and fail closed to avoid auth mismatch. longer-term: update hub route-map to prefer region-local NAT pool for prefixes originating from region-tagged VPCs. also allocate region-specific SNAT pools and pin by source VPC.
netops: confirmed — we can push a quick route-map to prefer next-hop from us-east for that customer's IP range. I'll schedule a controlled change to NAT allocation to avoid swapping floating IPs between regions.
raj: for repro steps in ticket: 1) configure VPC peering + hub NAT 2) force BGP path preference by withdrawing us-east med -> observe SNAT public IP move to eu 3) send requests with x-redwood-region header -> observe served-region mismatch and 401s. include curl & tcptraceroute outputs.
maya: copying mitigation + repro into support ticket and notifying customer of planned maintenance window. thanks. :thumbsup:
netops: will post the change window and roll back plan here once scheduled.
eli: follow-up: add an internal alert when served-region != requested-region more than 1% of 5m window — can add to Redwood Console per-route SLOs.
maya: noted, leaving thread open until netops confirms change done.
